summary: The candidate correctly bounds the full-matrix FP8-to-MXFP4 conversion allocation and preserves exact output bytes. On gfx950 the independent incremental peak fell 49.66%. The unavailable two-node GB10 model startup prevents claiming the original scheduler OOM is fully resolved.

tests.what_was_measured: Real checked-out base conversion on gfx950: 2,657,092,096-byte incremental peak for FP8 [4096,8192], with output checksums retained.
Candidate regression suite: 10 tests passed, covering chunking, packing layout, numerical round trips, grouped input, partial final scale rows, and invalid K alignment.
Candidate conversion on the identical seeded gfx950 input: 1,337,459,200-byte incremental peak (49.66% lower), identical packed and scale checksums.
Independent byte-exact comparison with the old algorithm across partial blocks, multidimensional/grouped shapes, alternate block sizes, and invalid K.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the real conversion; raw measurements are in base_gpu_conversion.txt and candidate_gpu_conversion.txt.

remaining_counterexamples: The original 2x NVIDIA GB10/SM120 distributed launch with the 156.31 GiB checkpoint was not available and may still exceed 121 GB per node.
Host anonymous RSS and unified-memory peak were not measured on GB10; the gfx950 allocator result does not prove the scheduler avoids the kernel OOM killer.
Concurrent checkpoint/H2D staging and loader-thread memory are outside this patch and may remain sufficient to OOM.
The SM12x-only b12x backend and its final packed-weight consumer were not executable on AMD gfx950.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA GB10/SM120, second node, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp weights, CUDA 13 container, b12x runtime, NCCL/RoCE setup, or full serving path. The change is Python-only, so no native rebuild was applicable.
